title: Latent Variable Estimation in Bayesian Black-Litterman Models
source_version: PMLR volume 267 published original; retrieved exact supplied PDF URL
summary: Incorrect Student-t degrees of freedom in the FIV approximation and a false predictive ground-truth collapse affect theoretical model properties. Released SLP code uses predictive covariance in the mean, with historical experimental effect unresolved. Reported average percentage improvements match table arithmetic.
limitations: No author code, optimizer or backtest executed; no historical empirical attribution established.
Actual PDF is 28 pages; source manifest's 52 is an extraction-control-character artifact preserved separately.
Full joint-model interpretation of the FIV mixture remains Needs Evidence.
Separate OpenReview attachments unavailable; later revisions/errata not independently inspected.
All main and applicable appendix text read, but not all background results and implementation files independently verified.

problems.title: FIV Normal–inverse-Wishart marginal has wrong degrees of freedom
problems.source_location: Corollaries 3.3.1–3.3.2 p.8; Lemma D.3 p.18; E.5 p.23; Appendix A p.14
problems.claim: Normal mean with IW(Psi',nu') covariance has t_nu' marginal and scale Psi'/(nu'-m+1).
problems.assumptions: theta|S~N(mu',S), S~IW(Psi',nu'), fixed mu', Psi' positive definite, nu'>m-1; use density D.8.
problems.check: Integrating yields kernel (1+u'Psi'^-1u)^(-(nu'+1)/2), hence kappa=nu'-m+1 and scale Psi'/kappa. For m=2,nu'=5,Psi'=I, true covariance I/2 versus printed 5I/12. IW mean is Psi'/(nu'-m-1), requiring nu'>m+1; Appendix A instead uses the t scale as its mean.
problems.result: Core approximate predictive distribution and prior moment wrong as stated.
problems.counterevidence: m=1 degrees coincide; no claim that the SLP experiments use FIV. The paper explicitly calls the FIV hierarchy an approximation, but the integral under its stated hierarchy is still exact and incorrect.
problems.impact: Major for FIV predictive derivation; no direct claim about SLP benchmark validity.

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Physically viewed p.18: the IW exponent in (D.8) is -(nu'+m+1)/2; the lemma explicitly names nu' as degrees of freedom, so this is not a hidden parameter convention. Corollary 3.3.2 fixes mu', which is the hierarchy being tested.
independent_check.decisive_check: Multiplication by the Gaussian contributes |S|^-1/2. The resulting IW integral has index nu'+1, hence determinant power -(nu'+1)/2. The determinant lemma yields (1+u'Psi^-1u)^(-(nu'+1)/2), so matching the t kernel forces kappa=nu'-m+1 and scale Psi/kappa. For m=2,nu'=5 the true covariance is (4/2)*(I/4)=I/2, while the printed t5 covariance is (5/3)*(I/4)=5I/12. The implied IW mean requires nu'>m+1 and denominator nu'-m-1, confirming the p.14 error.
independent_check.alternatives_and_scope: The calculation pertains to the stipulated approximate hierarchy, not proof of its approximation quality. m=1 masks the degrees-of-freedom error; SLP experiments do not depend directly on this FIV marginal. Major is supported for the core FIV predictive derivation. The stated repaired distribution and moment follow exactly within that hierarchy.

problems.title: Perfect views do not eliminate intrinsic predictive noise
problems.claim: Omega tends to zero and accurate classical views imply predictive returns converge to delta_rstar.
problems.assumptions: Scalar P=1, Sigma=Sigma0=OmegaF=1, theta0=feature_center=0, gamma=1, alpha=beta=0, q=rstar=2, Omega=epsilon>0.
problems.check: mu=2/(1+2epsilon), V=epsilon/(1+2epsilon); predictive law N(mu,1+V) converges to N(2,1), not delta_2 (different characteristic function). A rank-deficient P also leaves unobserved parameter uncertainty.
problems.counterevidence: Latent theta does collapse with full-rank exact views; P=I in practical appendix avoids rank issue but not intrinsic return noise.
problems.impact: Major for a model property explicitly used in the main conclusion; empirical SLP comparisons not refuted.

correction.statement: For full column rank P, Omega=epsilon Omega1 positive definite scaling and bounded other terms, theta tends to delta_rstar, while predictive r tends to N(rstar,Sigma); point-mass prediction also requires Sigma to zero.

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Remark 3.3 claims a predictive Dirac measure with no Sigma->0 assumption and is repeated in the p.9 conclusion. Scalar positive-definite covariances with gamma=1 and accurate q meet every displayed hypothesis.
independent_check.decisive_check: Recompleted the scalar square: precision 2+1/epsilon, latent mean 2/(1+2epsilon), variance epsilon/(1+2epsilon). Convolving independent N(0,1) return noise gives limiting N(2,1); the limiting characteristic function modulus at t=1 is exp(-1/2), rather than 1 for a point mass. With rectangular P=(1,0), only the first precision diverges; the other variance stays 1/2.
independent_check.alternatives_and_scope: Full-column-rank accurate views with common epsilon scaling recover latent theta and a noisy predictive Gaussian, exactly the restricted repair stated. P=I avoids nonidentifiability but not the retained Sigma. Core recovery property is false; no claim that empirical SLP gains are refuted.
independent_check.result: Major claim-level defect and restricted repair supported.

problems.title: Released mean uses predictive covariance multiplier
problems.claim: Released BL mean computation corresponds to the proposed posterior mean.
problems.assumptions: Sigma=Sigma0=diag(1,4), OmegaF=I, theta0=0, feature center=(1,1), all matrices positive definite; static formula check only.
problems.check: Correct Vb=(.5,.8), released (Sigma+V)b=(1.5,4.8). Positive long-only Sharpe weights are respectively (2/3,1/3) and (1/2,1/2).
problems.result: Confirmed release-level theoretical mismatch; historical benchmark provenance Needs Evidence.
problems.counterevidence: Pinned repository is a later refactor and its older file is not proof of which code generated the paper. No original experiment rerun.
problems.impact: Minor release-level finding; unknown historical effect not promoted to Major.

correction.statement: Use middle_inv @ rhs for mean while retaining adjusted_cov as predictive covariance.

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Read the actual frozen source lines 194-205 and old_version lines 226-239, and matched both file hashes to code_inspection.json. No author code executed. Both use Sigma+V as the multiplier of the precision-weighted vector.
independent_check.decisive_check: Independently evaluated the diagonal example: V=diag(1/2,4/5); b=(1,1); means (1/2,4/5) versus (3/2,24/5). Using C=diag(3/2,24/5), C^-1*correct_mean=(1/3,1/6), normalized to (2/3,1/3); released mean gives direction (1,1), normalized to halves. All weights are feasible and positive.
independent_check.alternatives_and_scope: A later refactor and older file do not establish the historical producing implementation. The release mismatch is Minor with historical effect unresolved. Substituting V for C in the mean restores the stated posterior identity only.
independent_check.result: Release-level discrepancy and bounded repair supported; historical effect remains Needs Evidence.

problems.title: Predictive corollary precision/inverse omissions
problems.claim: The displayed corollaries follow their preceding Gaussian posteriors.
problems.assumptions: P=Sigma0=OmegaF=Omega=1, zero centers, q=1, gamma=2 for M-BL; Sigma0=OmegaF=1, theta0=0, feature center=1 for SLP.
problems.check: M-BL precision is 6, mean1/3 and latent variance1/6, versus displayed precision3, mean2/3 and variance1/3. SLP printed GF*b=2 versus correct inverse product1/2.
problems.counterevidence: Adjacent theorems and proofs give correct expressions; gamma=1 avoids first discrepancy.
problems.impact: Minor, no additional empirical dependency established.

correction.statement: Restore gamma^2 in M-BL precision and (GF)^-1 in SLP mean.

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: The p.5 corollary drops gamma squared although its antecedent theorem retains it; p.7 multiplies by GF although Theorem 3.2 on p.6 uses its inverse. No special gamma=1 restriction is imposed on the former corollary.
independent_check.decisive_check: With gamma=2 and unit scalar covariances, the squared-residual quadratic gives precision 1+1+4=6, linear term 2, mean 1/3. The printed precision is 3 and produces 2/3. With GF=2 and b=1 the other printed mean is 2 instead of 1/2. Correcting these two symbols exactly recovers the Gaussian completed squares.
independent_check.alternatives_and_scope: Adjacent theorems give the correct formulas and gamma=1 hides one error. No further experimental dependency is established, so Minor rather than an additional Major is appropriate.
